title: Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem
alloyReason: Grade 2 CP-Ti (UNS R50400) is selected for this hydrogen hardware application prioritizing formability and corrosion resistance over strength. With 40% elongation and excellent weldability, its natural TiO2 passivation provides immunity to pitting in chlorides up to 260C. This rationale is driven by high-pressure hydrogen valve stem (grade 23 eli) and fat life requirements.
process: Closed-die forging net shape for hydrogen hardware geometry
CNC precision machining with 0.5mm corner radius
TIG welding all positions with 0.5mm corner radius
DPI dye penetrant inspect with 0.5mm corner radius
surfaceTreatment: Thermal oxidation 700C 2h in air to grow controlled 300nm TiO2 barrier layer for H2 permeation reduction — tailored for highpressure hydrogen valve application
inspection: UT volumetric full matrix (highpressure hydrogen verified)
commonFailures: Irradiation embrittlement in flux >1e18 n/cm2 - mitigated by fine equiaxed alpha (ASTM 8+) microstructure — critical for highpressure hydrogen valve performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem suitable for High-pressure hydrogen valve stem (Grade 23 ELI)?
faq.a: Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem uses Grade 2 CP-Ti because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address hydrogen hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for highpressure hydrogen valve requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. highpressure hydrogen valve components require Thermal oxidation 700C 2h in air to grow controlled 300nm TiO2 barrier layer for H2 permeation reduction — tailored for highpressure hydrogen valve application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Hydrogen Storage Valve Stem includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet highpressure hydrogen valve specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for H2 valve stem / Hydrogen valve hydrogen hardware components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
